// migrateTenants: migrate.mjs only touches the global schema. Per-tenant tables are applied at provisioning for NEW tenants, so an added tenant-template file would be missing for every EXISTING customer until migrate-tenants.mjs runs. It is idempotent, so running it on every boot is safe.
// seed: --seed is deliberate. The reference data in database/seeds is the framework catalogue and its 500+ controls, which is not optional content: without it framework_data.framework_controls is empty and adopting a framework creates nothing, silently. Every seed uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so re-running is safe, and controls added to the library in a later release land on deploy instead of needing a manual step someone will forget.
// startCommand: Must be wrapped in `sh -c`. backend/Dockerfile declares ENTRYPOINT [dumb-init, --], so Railway appends the start command as ARGV to that entrypoint rather than running it through a shell. Unwrapped, the `&&` and everything after it are passed as arguments to migrate.mjs, which ignores them and exits 0 — the container then dies before the server ever starts, and the healthcheck fails. render.yaml uses the same sh -c form.

deploy.startCommand: sh -c "node scripts/migrate.mjs --seed && node scripts/migrate-tenants.mjs && node dist/server.js"
